title: Partial-frame reconciliation and fuzzy-schema tolerance acceptance
creator: Maya Chen
description: Define acceptance criteria, tests, and rollout plan for a reconciliatory streaming protocol that tolerates partial/fragmented frames, supports fuzzy schema matching during resume/reconnect, and provides deterministic tool/function-calling semantics when frames are incomplete or reordered.
background: Customers have reported failures when long streamed structured responses include partial JSON frames due to network interruptions, client reconnects, or model re-rolls. Current behavior often results in dropped tool calls, duplicate invocation, or failed parsing on the client. This PRD formalizes a protocol for: (1) detecting and reconciling partial frames, (2) using schema-aware fuzzy matching to repair small deviations, and (3) ensuring idempotent, observable tool/function calls across reconnects.
scope:
- Implement server-side emission of lightweight reconciliation metadata (sequence id, frame checksums, schema_version, last_commit_index) alongside streamed frames.
- Define fuzzy-schema rules and prioritized repair heuristics for common deviations (trailing commas, missing quotes, small key typos).
- Guarantee idempotent tool/function-call semantics via replay tokens and call anchors.
- Add telemetry and dashboards for reconciliation success/failure and repair classification.
- Provide acceptance tests and e2e test harness for common failure modes.
out_of_scope: - Full language-model retraining or model-side emission guarantees.\n- Client SDKs for every language (we will ship reference Node/Python examples only).\n- Persistent storage semantics for resumed sessions beyond the reconciliation window (long-term archival is separate).
acceptance_criteria:
1) Reconciliation metadata is present: every streamed chunk emitted to clients includes a reconciliation header containing: sequence_id, chunk_index, schema_version (string), chunk_crc (hex), and optional commit_hint (string).

2) Partial-frame detection and resume: on reconnect, the server must accept a last_seen sequence_id/commit_hint from the client and produce a deterministic reconciliation plan: if the server identifies overlapping data it will emit a 'replay' section that marks frames as REPLAY/APPEND/REPLACE.

3) Fuzzy-schema tolerance rules: the platform must apply a deterministic set of repair heuristics (applied in order) for small deviations: (a) fix trailing commas, (b) convert single to double quotes where safe, (c) insert missing closing braces/brackets if a single token missing, (d) map key typos within a Levenshtein distance <=2 to the nearest schema key if unambiguous. Repairs applied must be logged and returned in the final metadata.

4) Tool/function call idempotency: each tool invocation emitted in-stream must include a call_anchor token (uuid) and a call_signature (model_prompt_hash + schema_version + call_anchor). On replay, the server must suppress duplicate executions when call_signature matches a previously executed signature and must return the cached call result.

5) Failure classification and fallback: if fuzzy repair fails or is ambiguous, the server must emit an explicit ERROR_FRAME event (with error_code and human_summary) and a deterministic fallback policy: (a) best-effort-parse (partial JSON envelope with repair_suggestions) OR (b) abort-and-report. The chosen policy is configurable per-customer but must default to (a) for self-serve customers and (b) for enterprise customers with strict schema enforcement.

6) Telemetry and SLOs: reconciliation success rate must be >= 99% for synthetic network interruption tests (see test_plan). The platform must surface: reconciliation_attempts, repairs_applied_count, repair_type_breakdown, suppressed_duplicate_calls, and ambiguous_repair_rate.

7) Observability surface: Console must show per-route reconciliation health (last 7d) and allow drilldown to sample events with raw emitted frames and the reconciliation diff.

8) Backwards compatibility: existing clients that do not send last_seen must continue to receive streaming frames unchanged. Reconciliation metadata is additive and safe to ignore for older SDKs.

9) Security: reconciliation metadata must not leak PII or secrets. All call_anchor tokens must be opaque and rotation-safe.

10) E2E tests pass: the test_plan (below) must run in CI and all cases must pass deterministically across 10 seeds of network jitter.
api_contract:
- Emitted stream envelope: each data chunk is preceded by a JSON reconciliation header prefixed with a deterministic delimiter (e.g., 'RIHDR v1'). Header fields: sequence_id (string), chunk_index (int as string), schema_version (string), chunk_crc (hex), commit_hint (string|null).
- Tool call object: {"call_anchor": "uuid", "call_payload": <opaque>, "call_signature": "hash"} (serialized to the stream).
- Resume handshake: client -> server: {last_sequence_id, last_commit_hint, client_session_id}. Server -> client: reconciliation plan stream entries of type {action: REPLAY|APPEND|REPLACE, sequence_id, chunk_index, payload_or_diff}.
- Note: All fields above are plain JSON strings in the header; payloads may be chunked. The header schema_version must match the model-serving registry.
streaming_semantics:
- Atomicity window: frames are considered reconcilable within a sliding window of last N sequence_ids (configurable, default 64). Frames older than the window are treated as immutable and will not be patched.
- Ordering guarantees: within a sequence_id ordering is preserved; across reconnects server will present data in a deterministic order according to sequence_id then chunk_index.
- Checksum enforcement: chunk_crc mismatch triggers a REPAIR_ATTEMPT; if CRC cannot be reconciled, an ERROR_FRAME is emitted with error_code=CRC_MISMATCH.
- Checkpointing: servers may optionally emit periodic COMMIT markers with commit_id and committed_index to make fast resumes cheaper.
- Streaming rate and backpressure: reconciliation metadata must be small (<512 bytes) and not materially affect streaming throughput. Batching of headers is allowed for high-throughput routes.
error_modes_and_recovery:
- CRC_MISMATCH: attempt fuzzy repairs; if unsuccessful, emit ERROR_FRAME and provide repair_suggestions.
- AMBIGUOUS_REPAIR: do not auto-apply; emit ERROR_FRAME with multiple suggested repairs and a chosen fallback policy (best-effort or abort).
- DUPLICATE_CALL_DETECTED: suppress execution and return cached response and mark metric suppressed_duplicate_calls++.
- MISSING_SCHEMA_VERSION: treat as schema_v0; if repair heuristic required, tag as legacy_repair.
- CLIENT_MALFORMED_RESUME: reject resume request with 400 and provide guidance: required fields.
- SERVER_SIDE_RECONCILIATION_FAILURE: capture diagnostic bundle and mark incident for P0 if rate > 0.5% of requests in a 15m window.
test_plan:
Test cases to run in CI and pre-release canary: 
1) Network-interruption-resume: introduce single mid-stream TCP drop; client reconnects providing last_sequence_id; verify deterministic replay path and no duplicate tool execution.
2) Truncated-json-frame: simulate missing trailing brace; verify fuzzy repair fixes or returns ERROR_FRAME depending on ambiguity.
3) Key-typo-repair: emit frame with 'usre_id' instead of 'user_id'; verify mapping under Levenshtein <=2 when unambiguous.
4) CRC mismatch detection: flip a byte on a chunk; ensure CRC_MISMATCH route triggers repair attempt and logs.
5) Duplicate call suppression: simulate server re-emitting a call with same call_signature; ensure only one execution recorded.
6) Backpressure/high-throughput: stream 50 tokens/sec with header batching; verify header sizes <512 bytes and <5% throughput overhead.
7) Ambiguity stress test: craft payloads that produce >1 repair suggestion; ensure ERROR_FRAME and metric increment.
8) Old-client compatibility: client that ignores reconciliation header must still parse non-reconciled frames successfully.
Each test includes 10 randomized seeds for jitter; acceptance requires 100% deterministic pass across seeds except where ambiguity is expected and validated.
telemetry: Emit the following metrics (per-route and aggregated): reconciliation_attempts, reconciliation_successes, repairs_applied, repair_type_{trailing_comma,single_quote,missing_brace,key_map,other}, ambiguous_repair_count, suppressed_duplicate_calls, error_frame_count, average_repair_latency_ms. Provide a sample dashboard and an alert rule: if ambiguous_repair_rate > 0.2% over 1h, create an Ops alert. Tag events with schema_version and route for drilldown.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature gated behind account-level flag 'reconciliatory_streaming_v2'. 2) Enable for internal test accounts and SRE (canary) for 24h. 3) Gradual rollout: 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% over 7 days if key metrics (reconciliation_success_rate, repair_latency, suppressed_duplicate_calls) are within thresholds. 4) If ambiguous_repair_rate spikes or customer-impact errors observed, pause rollout and revert flag. 5) Offer an enterprise strict mode toggle that enforces abort-on-ambiguity.\nSupport: provide feature-flag dashboard and kill-switch.
notes: Scope changed from original PRD: removed automatic client SDK upgrades (clients remain opt-in) and added explicit commit_hint to reduce resume ambiguity. PM/Eng trade-offs discussed: aggressive fuzzy repair increases success but risks silent data changes — decision is to always emit repair metadata and keep repairs visible for audit. Security review must sign off on token obfuscation approach before release.\nOpen questions: acceptable default sliding window size (propose 64), and whether to prioritize latency or repair thoroughness for low-tier routes.
